source_text:
108 Ἀνὴρ σοφὸς ἐρευνήσει λόγους θεοῦ, ὁ δὲ ἄσοφος καταγελάσεται αὐτῶν.
109 Ὁ μισῶν γνῶσιν θεοῦ καὶ ἀπωθούμενος θεωρίαν αὐτοῦ ὅμοιός ἐστι τῷ
λόγχῃ νύσσοντι τὴν καρδίαν αὑτοῦ.
110 Κρείσσων γνῶσις τριάδος ὑπὲρ γνῶσιν ἀσωμάτων καὶ θεωρία αὐτῆς ὑπὲρ
λόγους πάντων τῶν αἰώνων.
111 Πολιὰ γερόντων πραΰτης, ζωὴ δὲ αὐτῶν γνῶσις ἀληθείας.
112 Νέος πραῢς πολλὰ ὑποφέρει, ὀλιγόψυχον δὲ γέροντα τίς ὑποίσεται; εἶδον
ὀργίλον γέροντα ἐπαιρόμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου αὐτοῦ, ἐλπίδα δὲ μέντοι μᾶλλον ἔσχεν ὁ
νέος αὐτοῦ.
113 Ὁ σκανδαλίζων κοσμικοὺς οὐκ ἀτιμώρητος ἔσται, καὶ ὁ παροξύνων
αὐτοὺς ἀτιμάζει τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ.
114 Ταράσσοντα ἐκκλησίαν κυρίου ἐξαναλώσει πῦρ, ἀνθιστάμενον δὲ ἱερεῖ
καταπίεται γῆ.
115 Ὁ ἀγαπῶν μέλισσαν φάγεται κηρίον αὐτῆς καὶ ὁ συνάγων αὐτὴν
πλησθήσεται πνεύματος.
116 Τίμα τὸν κύριον καὶ γνώσῃ λόγους ἀσωμάτων, καὶ δούλευε αὐτῷ καὶ
δείξει σοι λόγους αἰώνων.
117 Χωρὶς γνώσεως οὐχ ὑψωθήσεται καρδία, καὶ δένδρον οὐκ ἀνθήσει ἄνευ
ποτοῦ. 118 Σάρκες Χριστοῦ πρακτικαὶ ἀρεταί, ὁ δὲ ἐσθίων αὐτὰς γενήσεται ἀπαθής.
119 Αἷμα Χριστοῦ θεωρία τῶν γεγονότων καὶ ὁ πίνων αὐτὸ σοφισθήσεται ὑπ'
αὐτοῦ.
120 Στῆθος κυρίου γνῶσις θεοῦ, ὁ δ' ἀναπεσὼν ἐπ' αὐτὸ θεολόγος ἔσται.
121 Γνωστικὸς καὶ πρακτικὸς ὑπήντησαν ἀλλήλοις, μέσος δὲ ἀμφοτέρων
εἱστήκει κύριος.
122 Ὃς ἐκτήσατο ἀγάπην, ἐκτήσατο θησαυρόν, ἔλαβε δὲ χάριν παρὰ κυρίου.
123 ∆όγματα δαιμόνων ἐπιγινώσκει σοφία, πανουργίαν δὲ αὐτῶν ἐξιχνιάζει
φρόνησις.
124 Μὴ ἀθετήσῃς δόγματα ἅγια, ἃ ἔθεντο οἱ πατέρες σου, πίστιν δὲ
βαπτίσματός σου μὴ ἐγκαταλίπῃς καὶ μὴ ἀπώσῃ σφραγῖδα πνευματικήν, ἵνα γένηται
κύριος ἐν σῇ ψυχῇ καὶ σκεπάσῃ σε ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κακῇ.
125 Λόγοι αἱρετικῶν ἄγγελοι θανάτου, καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος αὐτοὺς ἀπολεῖ τὴν
ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν.
126 Νῦν οὖν, υἱέ, ἄκουέ μου, καὶ μὴ προσέλθῃς θύραις ἀνδρῶν ἀνόμων μηδὲ
περιπατήσῃς ἐπὶ παγίδων αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ ἀγρευθῇς. ἀπόστησον δὲ σὴν ψυχὴν ἀπὸ
γνώσεως ψευδοῦς. καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ πλεονάκις λελάληκα πρὸς αὐτούς, σκοτεινοὺς δὲ
λόγους αὐτῶν ἐξιχνίασα, καὶ ἰὸν ἀσπίδων εὕρηκα ἐν αὐτοῖς. οὐκ ἔστι φρόνησις καὶ
οὐκ ἔστι σοφία ἐν λόγοις αὐτῶν. πάντες οἱ δεχόμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολοῦνται, καὶ οἱ
ἀγαπῶντες αὐτοὺς πλησθήσονται κακῶν. εἶδον ἐγὼ πατέρας δογμάτων αὐτῶν καὶ
ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ συνέβαλον αὐτοῖς. ἐχθροὶ γὰρ κυρίου ἀπήντησάν μοι καὶ δαίμονες ἐν
λόγοις ἠγωνίσαντο πρός με καὶ οὐκ εἶδον φῶς ἀληθινὸν ἐν ῥήμασιν αὐτῶν.
127 Ἀνὴρ ψευδόμενος ἐκπεσεῖται θεοῦ, ἀπατῶν δὲ τὸν πλησίον αὐτοῦ
ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς κακά.
128 Κρείσσων παράδεισος θεοῦ ὑπὲρ κῆπον λαχανίας καὶ ποταμὸς κυρίου
ὑπὲρ ποταμὸν μέγαν ἐπισκοτοῦντα τῇ γῇ.
5
129 Ἀξιοπιστότερον ὕδωρ οὐράνιον ὑπὲρ ὕδωρ Αἰγυπτίων σοφῶν
ἀντλούντων ἐκ γῆς.
130 Ὃν τρόπον οἱ τοὺς τροχοὺς ἀναβαίνοντες κάτω εἶσιν, οὕτως οἱ ὑψοῦντες
λόγους αὐτῶν τεταπείνωνται ἐν αὐτοῖς.
131 Σοφία κυρίου ὑψοῖ καρδίαν, φρόνησις δὲ αὐτοῦ καθαίρει αὐτήν.
132 Λόγοι προνοίας σκοτεινοὶ καὶ δυσνόητοι κρίσεως θεωρίαι, ἀνὴρ δὲ
πρακτικὸς ἐπιγνώσεται αὐτούς.
133 Καθαίρων ἑαυτὸν ὄψεται φύσεις νοεράς, λόγους δὲ ἀσωμάτων
ἐπιγνώσεται μοναχὸς πραΰς.
134 Ὁ κτίσμα λέγων τὴν ἁγίαν τριάδα βλασφημεῖ θεὸν καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν τὸν
Χριστὸν αὐτοῦ οὐ γνώσεται αὐτόν.
135 Κόσμων θεωρίαι πλατύνουσι καρδίαν, λόγοι δὲ προνοίας καὶ κρίσεως
ὑψοῦσιν αὐτήν.
136 Γνῶσις ἀσωμάτων ἐπαίρει τὸν νοῦν καὶ τῇ ἁγίᾳ τριάδι παρίστησιν αὐτόν.
137 Μέμνησθε τοῦ δεδωκότος ὑμῖν ἐν κυρίῳ σαφεῖς παροιμίας, καὶ μὴ
ἐπιλάθησθε τῆς ταπεινῆς μου ψυχῆς ἐν καιρῷ προσευχῆς.

thought_title: Wisdom, Knowledge, and the Path of the Monk
orientation: Evagrius is closing his collection of sayings for monks in community, contrasting true knowledge of God with heretical teachings and urging the monk to hold fast to the faith he received.
pass_a_gloss: 108 A wise man will search out [the] words of God, but the unwise [man] will mock them. 109 The [one] hating knowledge of God and pushing away contemplation of him is like the [one] piercing his own heart with a spear. 110 Better [is] knowledge of [the] Trinity than knowledge of bodiless beings, and contemplation of it than [the] words of all the ages. 111 [The] grey hair of elders [is] gentleness, and their life [is] knowledge of truth. 112 A gentle young [man] endures many things, but a faint-hearted old [man]—who will endure [him]? I saw an irascible old [man] exalting himself on his throne, but his young [man] rather had hope. 113 The [one] scandalizing worldly [people] will not be unpunished, and the [one] provoking them dishonors his name. 114 [The one] troubling [the] church of [the] Lord—fire will consume [him], and [the one] resisting a priest—[the] earth will swallow [him]. 115 The [one] loving a bee will eat its honeycomb, and the [one] gathering it will be filled with spirit. 116 Honor the Lord and you will know [the] words of bodiless beings, and serve him and he will show you [the] words of [the] ages. 117 Without knowledge [the] heart will not be exalted, and a tree will not bloom without drink. 118 [The] flesh of Christ [is] active virtues, and the [one] eating them will become free from passions. 119 [The] blood of Christ [is] contemplation of the things that have come to be, and the [one] drinking it will be made wise by it. 120 [The] breast of [the] Lord [is] knowledge of God, and the [one] reclining on it will be a theologian. 121 A knower and an active [man] met each other, and [the] Lord stood in [the] middle of both. 122 [The one] who acquired love acquired a treasure, and received grace from [the] Lord. 123 Wisdom recognizes [the] doctrines of demons, and prudence tracks out their cunning. 124 Do not reject [the] holy doctrines which your fathers set down, and do not abandon [the] faith of your baptism and do not push away [the] spiritual seal, so that [the] Lord may be in your soul and may shelter you in [the] evil day. 125 [The] words of heretics [are] angels of death, and the [one] receiving them will destroy his own soul. 126 Now therefore, my son, hear me, and do not go to [the] doors of lawless men nor walk on their snares, so that you may not be caught. Keep your soul away from false knowledge. For indeed I have spoken to them many times, and I tracked out their dark words, and I found [the] venom of asps in them. There is no prudence and there is no wisdom in their words. All those receiving them will perish, and those loving them will be filled with evils. I saw [the] fathers of their doctrines and I met them in the desert. For enemies of [the] Lord met me, and demons contended against me in words, and I did not see true light in their sayings. 127 A lying man will fall away from God, and [the one] deceiving his neighbor will fall into evils. 128 Better [is] [the] paradise of God than a garden of vegetables, and [the] river of [the] Lord than a great river darkening the earth. 129 More trustworthy [is] heavenly water than [the] water of Egyptian wise [men] drawing from [the] earth. 130 In the manner [that] those climbing wheels are below, so those exalting their words have been humbled in them. 131 [The] wisdom of [the] Lord exalts [the] heart, and his prudence purifies it. 132 [The] words of providence [are] dark and [the] contemplations of judgment [are] hard to understand, but an active man will recognize them. 133 [The one] purifying himself will see intelligent natures, and a gentle monk will recognize [the] words of bodiless beings. 134 The [one] calling the Holy Trinity a creature blasphemes God, and the [one] rejecting his Christ will not know him. 135 [The] contemplations of [the] worlds widen [the] heart, and [the] words of providence and judgment exalt it. 136 Knowledge of bodiless beings lifts up the mind and presents it to the Holy Trinity. 137 Remember the [one] who gave you clear proverbs in [the] Lord, and do not forget my humble soul in [the] time of prayer.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'active life' for πρακτική; here πρακτικαί modifies ἀρεταί, so 'active virtues' keeps the adjective sense without the banned 'practical'.

The glossary bans 'the Trinity' for ἁγία τριάς; here the source has bare τριάς without ἁγία, so 'the Trinity' is used for the bare noun, while 'Holy Trinity' is reserved for the full phrase in 134 and 136.
The glossary requires 'freedom from passions' for ἀπάθεια; the adjective ἀπαθής is rendered as 'free from passions' to match the glossary sense.
The source uses the noun θεολόγος, and 'theologian' is the standard English equivalent; no glossary term covers it, so a plain rendering is used.
The glossary bans 'gnostic' for γνῶσις-related terms; 'a knower' renders the noun γνωστικός literally without importing the heretical sense.
The phrase refers to baptismal sealing; 'spiritual seal' is a literal rendering that preserves the adjective-noun structure.

bible_refs.note: ἄκουέ μου, υἱέ in 126 echoes the address of Proverbs 1:8 (ἄκουε, υἱέ, νόμους πατρός σου).
μὴ προσέλθῃς θύραις ἀνδρῶν ἀνόμων μηδὲ περιπατήσῃς ἐπὶ παγίδων αὐτῶν in 126 echoes Proverbs 4:14-15 (ὁδοὺς δὲ ἀνόμων μὴ ἐπέλθῃς... μὴ παραπορεύου ἐπὶ παγίδων).
ἰὸν ἀσπίδων in 126 echoes Psalm 140:3 LXX (ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν).

pass_b_english: A wise man will search out the words of God, but a fool will mock them.
The one who hates knowledge of God and pushes away contemplation of Him is like a man piercing his own heart with a spear.
Knowledge of the Holy Trinity is better than knowledge of bodiless beings, and contemplation of the Holy Trinity is better than the words of all the ages.
The gray hair of elders is gentleness, and their life is knowledge of the truth.
A gentle young man endures many things, but who will endure a fainthearted old man? I have seen an irascible old man exalting himself on his throne, yet his young man had more hope than he did.
The one who scandalizes worldly people will not go unpunished, and the one who provokes them dishonors his own name.
Fire will consume the one who troubles the church of the Lord, and the earth will swallow the one who opposes a priest.
The one who loves a bee will eat its honeycomb, and the one who gathers it will be filled with the Spirit.
Honor the Lord and you will know the words of bodiless beings; serve Him and He will show you the words of the ages.
Without knowledge the heart will not be lifted up, and a tree will not bloom without drink.
The flesh of Christ is the active virtues, and the one who eats it will become free from passions.
The blood of Christ is contemplation of created things, and the one who drinks it will be made wise by it.
The breast of the Lord is knowledge of God, and the one who reclines on it will be a theologian.
A knower and a man of active life met one another, and the Lord stood between them both.
The one who has acquired love has acquired a treasure, and he has received grace from the Lord.
Wisdom recognizes the doctrines of demons, and prudence tracks out their cunning.

Do not reject the holy doctrines that your fathers established, and do not abandon the faith of your baptism; do not push away the spiritual seal, so that the Lord may be in your soul and shelter you on the evil day.
The words of heretics are angels of death, and the one who receives them destroys his own soul.

Now then, my son, listen to me: do not approach the doors of lawless men or walk on their snares, lest you be caught. Keep your soul far from false knowledge. For I have spoken to them many times, and I have tracked out their dark words, and I have found the venom of asps in them. There is no prudence and no wisdom in their words. All who receive them will perish, and those who love them will be filled with evils. I have seen the fathers of their doctrines, and I have encountered them in the desert. For enemies of the Lord met me, and demons contended with me in words, and I saw no true light in their sayings.
A man who lies will fall away from God, and the one who deceives his neighbor will fall into evils.
The paradise of God is better than a garden of vegetables, and the river of the Lord is better than a great river that darkens the earth.
Heavenly water is more trustworthy than the water of Egyptian wise men drawing from the earth.
Just as those who climb wheels go downward, so those who exalt their own words are humbled in them.
The wisdom of the Lord lifts up the heart, and His prudence purifies it.
The words of providence are dark, and the contemplations of judgment are hard to understand, but a man of active life will recognize them.
The one who purifies himself will see intelligent natures, and a gentle monk will recognize the words of bodiless beings.
The one who says the Holy Trinity is a creature blasphemes God, and the one who rejects His Christ will not know Him.
Contemplations of the worlds widen the heart, and words of providence and judgment lift it up.
Knowledge of bodiless beings raises the mind and presents it to the Holy Trinity.
Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord, and do not forget my humble soul in the time of prayer.

problems.why: glossary: banned rendering 'the active life' (use 'active life')
lint glossary: banned rendering of πρακτική; use 'active life' ('the active life')

edits.old: A knower and a man of the active life met one another
edits.new: A knower and a man of active life met one another

edits.old: but a man of the active life will recognize them
edits.new: but a man of active life will recognize them

fixed: Removed 'the' before 'active life' in two places to comply with the glossary ban on 'the active life'.

problems.why: νέος means 'young man', not specifically 'disciple'; no disciple relationship is stated
problems.ruling: νέος means 'young man,' not 'disciple'; no disciple relationship is stated in source.

problems.quote: The one who gathers the bee
problems.why: αὐτήν refers to honeycomb (κηρίον), not bee; 'gathers the bee' is absurd
problems.ruling: αὐτήν grammatically refers to κηρίον (honeycomb), not μέλισσαν (bee); 'gathers the bee' is nonsensical.

edits.old: yet his young disciple had more hope than he did.
edits.new: yet his young man had more hope than he did.

edits.old: and the one who gathers the bee will be filled with spirit.
edits.new: and the one who gathers it will be filled with spirit.

fixed: The two previously tried edits about 'active life' were not part of the confirmed problems and have not been changed.
The two confirmed problems have been corrected: 'his young disciple' to 'his young man', and 'gathers the bee' to 'gathers it'.

problems.quote: Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord
problems.source_quote: Μέμνησθε τοῦ δεδωκότος ὑμῖν ἐν κυρίῳ σαφεῖς παροιμίας
problems.why: English hides that this is Evagrius speaking in first person (δεδωκότος...μου ψυχῆς); 'the one who gave' makes it sound like God or another, not self-reference.
problems.fix: Remember me, who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord
problems.ruling: δεδωκότος...μου ψυχῆς: Evagrius self-refers; 'the one who gave' obscures this, misleading readers.

edits.old: Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord
edits.new: Remember me, who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord

problems.quote: Remember me, who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord
problems.source_quote: Μέμνησθε τοῦ δεδωκότος ὑμῖν ἐν κυρίῳ σαφεῖς παροιμίας
problems.why: English 'me, who gave' makes Evagrius the giver; Greek τοῦ δεδωκότος is third person, likely God.
problems.fix: Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord
problems.ruling: τοῦ δεδωκότος is articular participle, 'the one who gave'; 'me, who gave' wrongly makes speaker the giver, not God.

edits.old: Remember me, who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord
edits.new: Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord

fixed: The speaker problem is real: the Greek participle is third person, referring to God, not Evagrius. Changed 'me, who gave' to 'the one who gave'.

last_rejected.quote: The flesh of Christ is the active virtues
last_rejected.why: Glossary bans 'active life' for πρακτική; 'active virtues' violates this.
last_rejected.fix: The flesh of Christ is the virtues of the active life
last_rejected.ruling: πρακτικαὶ ἀρεταί = 'active virtues'; no glossary term ἐγκράτεια present here.

last_rejected.quote: The one who loves a bee will eat its honeycomb
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ ἀγαπῶν μέλισσαν φάγεται κηρίον αὐτῆς
last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'self-control' for ἐγκράτεια, but this is μέλισσα/bee, not ἐγκράτεια. No error here—wait, checking: this is about bee/honeycomb, no glossary issue. Removing.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter self-removed; μέλισσαν/κηρίον correctly rendered bee/honeycomb.

polish.changed: Clarified speaker transitions and pronoun references, smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud, and ensured technical terms remain consistent with the glossary while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Reader may not connect 'free from passions' with 'freedom from passions'.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'freedom from passions' throughout.

notes.why: Reader needs to know 'knowledge' alone often means 'knowledge of God' technically.
notes.fix: Clarify in orientation that bare 'knowledge' is technical term.

notes.why: Reader may not connect 'active soul/man' with 'active life' as technical term (πρακτική/praktikē).
notes.fix: Standardize or gloss: 'active life' for praktikē; 'active soul' unclear.

notes.why: Fine as noun/plural, but 'contemplation of created things' vs 'contemplation of Holy Trinity' need distinction.
Technical term for contemplation of angels/demons; hierarchy of knowledge unexplained.
notes.fix: Explain in orientation: angels/demons < Trinity in contemplative hierarchy.

notes.why: Obscure phrase; seems to mean hidden spiritual meanings or logoi of providence/judgment.
notes.fix: Explain as technical Evagrian term for spiritual realities.

notes.why: Technical term (νοερὰ φύσεις) for angels/demons as intellectual beings.
notes.fix: Gloss as 'angelic/demonic intelligences' or explain.

notes.why: Refers to Origenist controversy opponents; specific heretics unnamed.
notes.fix: Explain as anti-Origenist polemic, possibly targeting specific teachers.

notes.quote: Now then, my son, listen to me
notes.why: Sudden first-person autobiographical passage; speaker shifts from proverb to testimony.
notes.fix: Mark as personal testimony against heretics encountered in desert.

notes.quote: Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord
notes.why: Third-person self-reference or reference to another teacher? Unclear if Evagrius means himself.
notes.fix: Clarify: likely self-reference in modest third person.

notes.quote: The flesh of Christ is the active virtues
notes.why: Bold metaphor; 'active virtues' as Christ's flesh is eucharistic theology, may startle.
notes.fix: Explain as spiritualized eucharistic theology, not denial of real presence.

notes.quote: The blood of Christ is contemplation of created things
notes.why: More startling: contemplation of creatures as Christ's blood? Hierarchical theology.
notes.fix: Explain Evagrian sacramental mysticism: lower contemplation nourishes toward higher.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker in the first-person passages as Evagrius, made 'the Spirit' explicit in saying 115, and smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and reference.

notes.why: These render overlapping ascetic concepts inconsistently; 'freedom from passions' is the goal, but 'self-control' and 'prudence' sometimes translate related Greek terms without clear distinction.
notes.fix: Use 'freedom from passions' consistently for apatheia.

notes.why: Unclear if 'words of the ages,' 'words of all the ages,' and 'words of providence and judgment' are same or different mystical objects.
notes.fix: Clarify in notes if these are synonyms or distinct contemplative levels.

notes.why: Refers to specific heretics Evagrius debated, but none are named; 'fathers' here means founders, not spiritual fathers.
notes.fix: Note: 'fathers of doctrines' = founders of heresies, not monks' spiritual fathers.

notes.quote: Egyptian wise men drawing from the earth
notes.why: Alludes to Nile irrigation or pagan philosophers, unexplained.
notes.fix: Note: Likely refers to Egyptian priests/philosophers or Nile-based agriculture.

notes.quote: Now then, my son, listen to me
notes.why: Sudden shift to first-person autobiographical account of encountering heretics; speaker unclear (Evagrius? A persona? A father to son?).
notes.fix: Note: Here Evagrius speaks in his own voice, recounting his desert struggles with demons/heretics.

notes.quote: Remember the one who gave you clear proverbs in the Lord, and do not forget my humble soul
notes.why: Unclear who 'the one who gave you clear proverbs' is—Evagrius himself? Another teacher? God?
notes.fix: Note: Likely Evagrius referring to himself modestly, or to a teacher; 'my humble soul' confirms first-person ending.

notes.quote: A knower and a man of active life met one another, and the Lord stood between them both
notes.why: Paradoxical: if Lord stands between, they don't truly meet; meaning of 'knower' (gnostikos) and 'active life' (praktikos) unclear.
notes.fix: Note: Evagrian schema—contemplative and active stages are united in Christ.

notes.quote: Just as those who climb wheels go downward
notes.why: Nonsensical: climbing wheels should go upward; 'wheels' may mean 'ladders' or 'spheres' but image fails.
notes.fix: Possibly 'climb on wheels' = 'turn wheels' or 'spin wheels'; or emend to 'those who turn wheels'.

notes.quote: The one who loves a bee will eat its honeycomb, and the one who gathers it will be filled with spirit
notes.why: Filled with 'spirit' seems abrupt; probably 'filled with the Spirit' or 'filled with honey/spiritual sweetness'.
notes.fix: Capitalize 'Spirit' if Holy Spirit intended, or note 'spirit' = spiritual gift.

notes.quote: The breast of the Lord is knowledge of God, and the one who reclines on it will be a theologian
notes.why: 'Theologian' in modern sense is misleading; here means 'one who knows God mystically', not academic theologian.
notes.fix: Note: 'theologian' = mystic/contemplative of the Trinity, not scholar.

notes.why: Phrase appears twice with no explanation; reader cannot tell if it means teachings, prophecies, or cosmic mysteries.
notes.fix: Gloss as 'the spiritual mysteries embedded in the ages of creation' or similar.

notes.why: Recurring phrase; reader may not connect 'bodiless beings' with angels/demons without the introduction.
notes.fix: First occurrence should note: 'bodiless beings—i.e., angels and demons.'
